== Enshrined deities ==
The following three deities are enshrined.
; Main enshrined deity
:* '''{{ill|Shinatsuhiko|azb|شینات سوهیکو|es|Shinatsuhiko|fa|شینات سوهیکو|it|Shinatsuhiko|ja|シナツヒコ|mni|ꯁꯤꯅꯠꯁꯨꯍꯤꯀꯣ|ru|Синацухико-но ками|sv|Shinatsuhiko|zh|志那都比古神|qid=Q1073925|lt=Shinatsuhiko-no-Mikoto}}''' (しなつひこのみこと) - a wind deity. In shrine tradition, this deity is regarded as the husband or younger brother of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shinatobe-no-Mikoto}}, the enshrined deity of {{ill|Anesaki Shrine|ja|姉埼神社|sv|Anesaki-jinja|qid=Q11447235}}.
; Associated deities
:* {{ill|Kuma District, Kumamoto|ceb|Kuma-gun|fr|District de Kuma|it|Distretto di Kuma|ja|球磨郡|ko|구마군|lt|Kumos apskritis|pl|Powiat Kuma|zh|球磨郡|qid=Q1132476|lt=Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto}} (やまとたけるのみこと)
:* {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|es|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|fa|یاماتوهیمه نو میکوتو|fr|Yamatohime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|mni|ꯌꯃꯇꯣꯍꯤꯃꯦ-ꯅꯣ-ꯃꯤꯀꯣꯇꯣ|vi|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|zh|倭姬命|qid=Q4388732|lt=Yamatohime-no-Mikoto}} (やまとひめのみこと)

that {{ill|Kuma District, Kumamoto|ceb|Kuma-gun|fr|District de Kuma|it|Distretto di Kuma|ja|球磨郡|ko|구마군|lt|Kumos apskritis|pl|Powiat Kuma|zh|球磨郡|qid=Q1132476|lt=Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto}} encountered a violent storm at Hashirimizu Sea (the {{ill|Uraga Channel|ceb|Uraga Suidō|es|Canal de Uraga|fa|کانال اوراگا|fr|Chenal d'Uraga|ja|浦賀水道|nl|Straat van Uraga|pt|Canal de Uraga|tr|Uraga Kanalı|zh|浦賀水道|qid=Q723431}}) during his eastern expedition, but was able to land safely in Kazusa through the self-sacrifice of his consort {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ototachibana-hime}}. Shrine tradition says that at that time Ototachibana-hime prayed to the deity of {{ill|Tatsuta Taisha|abstract|Q246455|de|Tatsuta-Taisha|fr|Tatsuta-taisha|ja|龍田大社|ru|Тацута-тайся|sv|Tatsuta-taisha|zh|龍田大社|qid=Q246455}} in {{ill|Yamato Province|be|Ямата (правінцыя)|ca|Província de Yamato|ckb|پارێزگای یەماتۆ|cs|Provincie Jamato|de|Provinz Yamato|el|Επαρχία Γιαμάτο|es|Provincia de Yamato|fa|ولایت یاماتو|fi|Yamaton provinssi|fr|Province de Yamato|gl|Provincia de Yamato|hak|Yamato-koet|id|Provinsi Yamato|it|Yamato (provincia)|ja|大和国|ko|야마토국|lt|Jamato žemė|nl|Yamato (provincie)|no|Yamato (provins)|pt|Província de Yamato|ro|Provincia Yamato|ru|Ямато (провинция)|simple|Yamato Province|sk|Jamato (provincia)|sr|Провинција Јамато|th|แคว้นยามาโตะ|tr|Yamato (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ямато|ur|یاماتو صوبہ|zh|大和國|zh_min_nan|Yamato-kok|zh_yue|大和國|qid=Q907495}}, vowing to enshrine a wind-calming god if safe passage to Kazusa were granted; in accordance with her last wish, Yamato Takeru enshrined Shinatsuhiko-no-Mikoto here.

Shrine tradition also states that in the 57th year of Emperor Keiko, after Yamato Takeru's death,<ref>[http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=2052 Shimaana Shrine] (Jinja no Hiroba).</ref> Emperor Keiko, father of Yamato Takeru, visited places associated with Yamato Takeru's eastern campaign and jointly enshrined the divine spirits of Yamato Takeru-no-Mikoto and Yamatohime-no-Mikoto at this shrine.

The shrine once had close ties with the likewise Shikinaisha {{ill|Anesaki Shrine|ja|姉埼神社|sv|Anesaki-jinja|qid=Q11447235}}, and it is said the sacred palanquin traveled between the two shrines.

== Related site ==
[[File:Shimaana-jinja, former place.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Former shrine site}}{{small|The current shrine site is farther in beyond the {{ill|Uchibō Line|de|Uchibō-Linie|fa|خط اوچیبو|fr|Ligne Uchibō|it|Linea Uchibō|ja|内房線|ko|우치보선|ru|Линия Утибо|tl|Linyang Uchibō|zh|內房線|qid=Q1142964}} tracks.}}]]
* Former shrine site
*: Located about 200 meters north of the present site, on the far side of the railway line. It is traditionally transmitted as the former seat of Shimaana Shrine, and is said to have once covered a considerable area. Formerly there was a deep cave in the woods, and because a clear wind was said to always blow from it, it was considered an action place of Shinatsuhiko-no-Mikoto, the wind deity; the shrine name "Shimaana" is also said to derive from this{{Sfn|Anesaki Shrine and Shimaana Shrine (Kami-gami)|1984}}. Although no cave is confirmed today and the tradition cannot be verified, it has been suggested that the tradition may refer to the stone chamber of an ancient tumulus{{Sfn|Anesaki Shrine and Shimaana Shrine (Kami-gami)|1984}}.
